paper.title: Designing Decision Support Systems Using Counterfactual Prediction Sets

settings.name_in_paper: Finding the optimal conformal predictor (arms = alpha values) with counterfactual prediction sets
unmapped: Arms are m nested conformal prediction sets (alpha_i = 1 - i/(m+1)); the learner observes feature x_t and true label y_t after each round, which together with the nested structure and the counterfactual monotonicity assumption reveals rewards of other arms (counterfactual side information)
Counterfactual monotonicity assumption (Assumption 2) on the expert's SCM
settings.definition_quote: In our problem, each arm corresponds to a different parameter value $\alpha$ and, at each round $t$, a (potentially different) human expert receives a sample with feature vector $x_t$, picks a label value $\hat{y}_t$ from the prediction set $\Ccal_{\alpha_t}(x_t)$ provided by the conformal predictor with $\alpha_t \in \Acal$, and obtains a reward $\II\{ \hat{y}_t = y_t \} \in \{0, 1\}$. Here, we observe $x_t$ at the beginning of each round and $y_t$ and $\II\{ \hat{y}_t = y_t \}$ at the end of each round.

symbols.t_round: current round t <= T at which the regret is evaluated

conditions: T >= sqrt(K) (paper: T >= sqrt(m), m = calibration set size = number of arms)
ground truth label y_t observed at end of each round

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Given a calibration set $\Dcal_{\text{cal}} = \{ (x_i, y_i) \}_{i=1}^{m}$ and a maximum number of rounds $T \geq \sqrt{m}$, Counterfactual SE is guaranteed to achieve expected regret $\EE[R(t)] \leq O \left( \sqrt{t \log m \log T} \right)$ for any $t \leq T$.

results.notes: Number of arms m mapped to K. Regret R(T) defined via expected accuracies, so pseudo-regret. Feedback is bandit plus counterfactually inferred rewards (not expressible in vocabulary).

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit (m arms) with rewards in {0,1}, vanilla bandit feedback
